 Democrats sweep Monmouth County offices, ending 18-year Republican winning streak
 In a county Trump carried by 11 points, Democrats win two commissioner seats and unseat incumbent Surrogate Maureen Raisch
 By David Wildstein , November 03 2026 
 9:47 pm 
 Democrats scored a stunning upset in Monmouth County on Tuesday, winning two seats on the Board of County Commissioners and ousting an incumbent surrogate in a county that Donald Trump carried by 11 percentage points just two years ago.
 The Democratic sweep marks the party’s first countywide victories in Monmouth since 2008 and breaks a Republican hold on all five county commissioner seats that dates back to 2011.
 Democrat Anthony Cherry, a criminal defense attorney, defeated Republican Surrogate Maureen Raisch, who was seeking a second five-year term. With 484 of 485 election districts reporting, Cherry had 115,552 votes, or 51.04%, to Raisch’s 110,614 votes, or 48.86%, a margin of 4,938 votes.
 Raisch, a longtime Republican elected official who previously served two decades in Middletown municipal government, had won the surrogate’s office in 2021.
 In the commissioner race, Democrats Chelsey Tanner and Sofia Ugarte defeated Republican Commissioner Erik Anderson and Middletown Mayor Tony Perry, who was seeking to replace retiring Republican Commissioner Ross Licitra.
 Tanner, a nonprofit executive, led the field with 115,713 votes, followed by Ugarte, a community advocate, with 114,049. Anderson trailed with 111,332 votes.
 The victories give Democrats two seats on the five-member Board of County Commissioners, leaving Republicans with a narrow 3-2 majority.
